description:
Adjacent finding surfaced while closing fz-usm.6 (parity audit of the builtin
type-constructor registry).

world.rs (~line 3190-3247) has a second, independent name->Ty registry:
BuiltinValueFamily / ImplTargetKind::Builtin, used to classify a `defimpl
Protocol, for: X` target as one of the compiler's built-in ground value
families (List, Integer, Float, Atom, Binary, Map), matched by the
capitalized last dotted segment of the module name (from_name, ~line 3216).
This is a hand-maintained enum with its own name table, doing the same
conceptual job as resolve.rs's ConstructorEntry/CONSTRUCTORS -- minting a Ty
from a recognized builtin name -- but populated and keyed independently:

- Different case convention by design (Elixir module names are capitalized
  `List`/`Map`; type-position names are lowercase `list`/`map`) -- these are
  arguably different domains (protocol-impl-target names vs. type-annotation
  names), not simply the same lookup miscased. Whether they *should* be one
  registry, or are legitimately two, is the open question this ticket should
  answer.
- No Tuple family: `defimpl Enumerable, for: Tuple` falls through to the
  Nominal branch (nominal_impl_target_ty, ~line 2878) and is treated as an
  opaque nominal type rather than dispatching on the actual tuple value
  family -- a real functional gap (mirrors this epic's original "no map"
  symptom, but for tuple, at this third site). Also absent: Bool, Nil, Pid,
  Ref, Resource, Cpointer, Utf8, Never -- though not all of these obviously
  need a defimpl target (open question per name, not all necessarily gaps).
- `Map` was already present here (builtin_value_family_ty, ~line 3240 ->
  t.map_top()) before fz-usm.3 added `map` to the resolve.rs registry -- i.e.
  this site was already 2-for-1 ahead of the resolver on "map" before this
  epic started.

Proposed direction (not yet designed/authorized): decide whether
BuiltinValueFamily should be folded into (or derived from) CONSTRUCTORS -- if
so, whether by a case-insensitive/capitalize-first-letter bridge or by adding
an explicit "protocol-impl-target name" field per registry entry -- and, if
tuple dispatch is wanted, add a Tuple family with its Ty-minting rule.

VERIFY: a fixture asserting `defimpl Enumerable, for: Tuple` dispatches on the
tuple family (once/if the family is added) or is documented as an intentional
gap the way fz-usm.6 documents `tuple`'s absence from CONSTRUCTORS.
title: fz-usm follow-up: reconcile world.rs BuiltinValueFamily (defimpl target dispatch) with the resolve.rs CONSTRUCTORS registry
